authority_charter: All alerts are advisory, generated by a deterministic, rules-only evaluation engine following the M-AI Kernel condition grammar (see mai-kernel/lib/condition-evaluator.js). No AI judgment, no learning, no network calls. Human authority (Accountable Manager / Quality Manager, or delegated) controls all decisions. Alerts are not a substitute for FAA/EASA surveillance or a certification determination.
note_on_integration_status: This DIM is embedded directly in the static HTML tool (artifact/index-v2-fsa.html) as a clearly-labeled JS module. It is NOT yet wired to the live mai-kernel runtime (no DB-backed events/assessments/ledger, no adapter, no supersession tracking) because the host is a client-side-only static tool with no backend. This manifest is the canonical, version-controlled source of truth for the rules; the embedded copy in index-v2-fsa.html must be kept in sync with this file until true kernel wiring (Postgres adapter + mai_* schema) lands in a future backend build. Known divergence: SURV-002 is defined here for documentation completeness (a broader 'surveillance past due' rule independent of the renewal window) but is intentionally NOT included in the embedded HTML copy, to avoid firing a duplicate/overlapping alert alongside SURV-001 in the current single-station demo dataset. Reconcile before adding a second demo station whose data could make SURV-002 fire independently of SURV-001.

rules.finding_text: FAA/EASA surveillance is past due and the approval renewal window is closing within 60 days.
rules.resolution_hint: Contact the FSDO/competent authority immediately and book the surveillance appointment.

rules.finding_text: FAA/EASA surveillance cycle is past due.
rules.resolution_hint: Schedule surveillance as soon as possible; verify no renewal-window conflict.
limitations: Superseded in practice by SURV-001 when renewal window is also < 60 days; both rules may fire independently per the kernel's no-hardcoded-dispatch law (each rule is evaluated on its own merits).

rules.finding_text: Four or more corrective actions are open, increasing the risk of a compounded audit finding.
rules.resolution_hint: Prioritize closure of the oldest/highest-risk corrective actions before next surveillance.

rules.finding_text: At least one corrective action is past its due date.
rules.resolution_hint: Verify effectiveness and close the overdue action; accelerate evidence collection.

rules.finding_text: One or more certifying staff authorizations expire within 60 days.
rules.resolution_hint: Enroll affected staff in recurrent training now; consider contract certifying staff as a bridge.

rules.finding_text: One or more approved suppliers are in Red risk status.
rules.resolution_hint: Quarantine affected parts, audit the supplier's process, qualify a replacement vendor if needed.

rules.finding_text: AS9110C QMS maturity score is below the 75-point internal benchmark.
rules.resolution_hint: Conduct an AS9110C gap analysis and refresher training for the QMS team.

operator_grammar_source: mai-kernel/lib/condition-evaluator.js (is_null, not_null, is_empty, not_empty, eq, ne, in, length_gte, length_lt, date_before_today, date_after_today, linked_record_exists, linked_record_missing, all[], any[], not{})
known_limitations: length_gte/length_lt are used for numeric greater-than/less-than comparisons because the kernel grammar has no dedicated gt/lt operator; thresholds are expressed as the smallest/largest qualifying integer (e.g. length_gte: 4 means > 3).

No date_before_today/date_after_today rules are used yet because the station snapshot in this static demo stores pre-computed day counts rather than raw dates; a future backend integration should snapshot raw dates and let the kernel compute recency.

This manifest is evaluated client-side in the browser with no persistence, no supersession, no append-only ledger, and no tenant scoping — those are mai-kernel runtime guarantees (Design Laws 4, 7, 9) that require the Postgres adapter and are out of scope for a static HTML tool.
